## Overview

This document extends the enrichment analysis started interactively with
**MetaboAnalystR** (the R package underlying the MetaboAnalyst web server) to
all metabolomics datasets and directional contrasts in the study. We run
metabolite set over-representation analysis (MSEA/ORA) against the SMPDB
pathway library for six contrasts: significant metabolites at 9 and 15
months, each split into all/upregulated/downregulated subsets.

> **Interpretive caveat**: MetaboAnalystR's ORA tests against the full set of
> compounds in the SMPDB library as background, not against the 738
> metabolites actually measured on the Metabolon platform. This differs from
> the custom Fisher's exact ORA in Part 1, which correctly restricts the
> background to detected metabolites. Results here should be read as a
> complementary, curated-database perspective rather than a like-for-like
> replacement.

## Libraries

```{r}
#| label: load-libraries
#| echo: true

# Core packages plus MetaboAnalystR for pathway-level enrichment
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(pals)
library(patchwork)
library(ggrepel)
library(scales)
library(MetaboAnalystR)
```

## Data Loading

```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| echo: true

# Load cleaned metabolomics data from Part 1
input_dir <- here("output", "01_data_loading_and_pathway_analysis")

met_9m  <- readRDS(file.path(input_dir, "met_9m_clean.rds"))
met_15m <- readRDS(file.path(input_dir, "met_15m_clean.rds"))

cat("Loaded:", nrow(met_9m), "met 9m,", nrow(met_15m), "met 15m\n")
```

## Building the Six Contrasts

For each timepoint we define three metabolite sets: all significant
metabolites (p < 0.05), and the upregulated/downregulated subsets. Splitting
by direction lets ORA highlight pathways driven specifically by accumulation
or depletion, which a single undirected hit list would mask.

```{r}
#| label: build-contrasts
#| echo: true

# Clean metabolite names (strip Metabolon confidence asterisks) for name mapping
clean_names <- function(x) {
  x |> stringr::str_remove_all("\\*$") |> stringr::str_trim() |> unique()
}

contrasts <- list(
  "9m \u2014 All Significant"  = met_9m  |> filter(significant) |> pull(biochemical) |> clean_names(),
  "9m \u2014 Upregulated"      = met_9m  |> filter(significant, log2fc > 0) |> pull(biochemical) |> clean_names(),
  "9m \u2014 Downregulated"    = met_9m  |> filter(significant, log2fc < 0) |> pull(biochemical) |> clean_names(),
  "15m \u2014 All Significant" = met_15m |> filter(significant) |> pull(biochemical) |> clean_names(),
  "15m \u2014 Upregulated"     = met_15m |> filter(significant, log2fc > 0) |> pull(biochemical) |> clean_names(),
  "15m \u2014 Downregulated"   = met_15m |> filter(significant, log2fc < 0) |> pull(biochemical) |> clean_names()
)

# Quick overview of contrast sizes
tibble(
  Contrast = names(contrasts),
  N_metabolites = map_int(contrasts, length)
) |> knitr::kable(caption = "Metabolite counts per contrast")
```

## MetaboAnalystR MSEA/ORA Workflow

MetaboAnalystR writes cache and library files to the current working
directory, so we point it at this script's output folder before running any
analyses and restore the original working directory afterwards.

```{r}
#| label: msea-ora-function
#| echo: true

# Run MetaboAnalystR name mapping + ORA against SMPDB pathways for one contrast
run_msea_ora <- function(compound_vec, contrast_label, msetlib = "smpdb_pathway",
                          min_size = 2) {
  mSet <- InitDataObjects("conc", "msetora", FALSE)
  mSet <- Setup.MapData(mSet, compound_vec)
  mSet <- CrossReferencing(mSet, "name")
  mSet <- CreateMappingResultTable(mSet)

  map_tbl <- mSet$dataSet$map.table
  n_mapped <- sum(!is.na(map_tbl[, "Match"]) & map_tbl[, "Match"] != "NA")

  mSet <- SetMetabolomeFilter(mSet, FALSE)
  mSet <- SetCurrentMsetLib(mSet, msetlib, min_size)
  mSet <- CalculateHyperScore(mSet)

  as.data.frame(mSet$analSet$ora.mat) |>
    tibble::rownames_to_column("pathway") |>
    dplyr::rename(raw_p = `Raw p`, holm_p = `Holm p`, fdr = FDR) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      contrast   = contrast_label,
      n_query    = length(compound_vec),
      n_mapped   = n_mapped,
      pct_mapped = n_mapped / length(compound_vec) * 100
    )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: run-all-contrasts
#| echo: true

# Point MetaboAnalystR at this script's output folder for cache/library files
output_dir <- here("output", "04_metaboanalystr_enrichment")
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
original_wd <- getwd()
setwd(output_dir)

# Run MSEA/ORA for all six contrasts against SMPDB pathways
ora_all <- imap_dfr(contrasts, ~ run_msea_ora(.x, .y))

# Restore the original working directory once MetaboAnalystR calls are done
setwd(original_wd)

cat("ORA completed for", n_distinct(ora_all$contrast), "contrasts,",
    n_distinct(ora_all$pathway), "unique SMPDB pathways tested\n")
```

### Name Mapping Rates

```{r}
#| label: mapping-rate-table
#| echo: true

# Compound name mapping success per contrast (from MetaboAnalystR's internal dictionary)
ora_all |>
  distinct(contrast, n_query, n_mapped, pct_mapped) |>
  arrange(contrast) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Compound name mapping rate by contrast")
```

## Figure: Top Pathways by Direction {.tabset}

Bar charts of the top 10 SMPDB pathways by raw p-value for each timepoint,
split into upregulated and downregulated metabolite subsets.

```{r}
#| label: direction-bar-function
#| echo: true

# Reusable bar chart of top pathways for a given timepoint's up/down contrasts
plot_direction_bars <- function(ora_data, timepoint_label) {
  plot_df <- ora_data |>
    filter(str_starts(contrast, timepoint_label), str_detect(contrast, "Up|Down")) |>
    mutate(
      direction = if_else(str_detect(contrast, "Up"), "Up", "Down"),
      neg_log10p = -log10(raw_p)
    ) |>
    group_by(direction) |>
    slice_max(neg_log10p, n = 10) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(pathway = fct_reorder(pathway, neg_log10p))

  ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = neg_log10p, y = pathway, fill = direction)) +
    geom_col(alpha = 0.85) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
    facet_wrap(~ direction, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(Up = "#d95f02", Down = "#1b9e77"), guide = "none") +
    labs(title = paste0("Top SMPDB Pathways \u2014 ", timepoint_label),
         subtitle = "MetaboAnalystR ORA, dashed line = raw p = 0.05",
         x = expression(-log[10]~"(raw p)"), y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Figure: Cross-Contrast Pathway Heatmap

A summary heatmap of the pathways most enriched across any contrast, showing
how significance shifts between timepoints and direction of change.

```{r}
#| label: fig-contrast-heatmap
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8

# Select top pathways by best (minimum) raw p-value across all contrasts
top_pathways <- ora_all |>
  group_by(pathway) |>
  summarise(min_p = min(raw_p), .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_min(min_p, n = 15) |>
  pull(pathway)

heatmap_data <- ora_all |>
  filter(pathway %in% top_pathways) |>
  mutate(
    neg_log10p = -log10(raw_p),
    sig_label = if_else(fdr < 0.1, "*", ""),
    contrast = factor(contrast, levels = names(contrasts)),
    pathway = fct_reorder(pathway, neg_log10p, .fun = max)
  )

p_contrast_heatmap <- ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = contrast, y = pathway, fill = neg_log10p)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sig_label), size = 5, vjust = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#b2182b",
                      name = expression(-log[10]~"(raw p)")) +
  labs(title = "SMPDB Pathway Enrichment Across Contrasts",
       subtitle = "Top 15 pathways by best raw p-value; * marks FDR < 0.1",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid = element_blank())
p_contrast_heatmap
```

       p_contrast_heatmap, width = 11, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

cat("All outputs saved to:", output_dir, "\n")
